Ciepielów Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ciepielów, Poland

Demolished. The Jewish cemetery of Ciepielów, on the town's eastern edge, likely dates to the late 18th century, though its exact founding is undocumented; the earliest confirmed references come from an 1839 topographic survey and 1846 burial-fee records, and the ground was fenced by 1870. By 1921, Ciepielów's 339 Jewish residents made up over a third of the town's population - nearly all were murdered at Treblinka by the Germans in late 1942. The wartime and postwar years saw the cemetery stripped of its tombstones and fence, and in 1964 Polish authorities formally closed it by ministerial order. Today the site is partly used as a wood yard and is otherwise overgrown, with no surviving gravestones or markers, though it remains listed on Poland's Provincial Register of Monuments.
